races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Tim Easterby dropping back from 9-10f assignments; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim is a useful weight advantage but this horse's good-going record at this trip is modest (0 wins from 13 similar runs) and the need to produce a sustained late run from the rear makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: Headgear note: visor fitted; David O'Meara's 8-year-old has decent good-going form (2W2P from 15) but has operated at 7f recently and the extra furlong at York is an open question — Mark Winn will need a strong pace to haul this horse into contention from the back of the field.

runners_data.name: Wild Nature
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter; Oisin Murphy is an outstanding tactical jockey for this role and Edward Bethell has had three runners in the past fortnight; the STYLE_FIT flag reminds that this is a horse being asked to front-run in a way that may not be its optimal role, but the position itself is straightforward if Murphy dictates cleanly.

runners_data.name: Sujet
runners_data.note: Zak Wheatley partners this Declan Carroll-trained 4-year-old who showed a place effort at 7f on good ground recently; a natural prominent type who will seek the early position but faces stiff competition for that berth from multiple rivals — Carroll's 14-day form is limited (1/16).

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Two wins in his last five starts for Chris Dwyer (0/7 in past 14 days); Silvestre De Sousa is an intelligent jockey who will look to position just off Wild Nature's shoulder — the drop to 1m from 8f runs is fine and the form on good ground is solid (2W5P).

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 4-year-old wears a hood and has placed consistently at 8-9f on good ground (2W7P from 15); Clifford Lee takes over and will look to sit behind the early pace — the habit of finishing in the first three at this trip in similar conditions makes this one of the more convincing prominent profiles.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has placed at 7-8f on good ground (1W3P); Kevin Stott is a smart jockey who will travel through the field from a hold-up position, and the consistent form string suggests a reliable competitor if the pace falls right.

runners_data.name: Cadarn
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 5-year-old has a tongue-tie and genuinely wants to race prominently, but the redistribution note is real — Shane Gray will likely find this horse squeezed out of its natural forward berth by more pace-minded rivals, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a meaningful discount on its prospects.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 6-year-old has won over 6f and placed at that trip for David Nolan but steps up to 1m here — the redistribution sees this natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield, which is not ideally disadvantageous at least, but the step in trip and 0/5 trainer form in 14 days is cautionary.

runners_data.name: Eligible
runners_data.note: The 10-year-old for Michael & David Easterby is a natural prominent racer, and Lewis Chalkley's 7lb claim is the headline positive; however, being bumped to midfield by the surfeit of pace types is a real obstacle for a horse of this age who needs to race on its own terms.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 3-year-old has two wins on soft and standard, but both his good-going runs have yielded 9th and 10th — Tom Marquand will look to position prominently, and the good-ground form concern (0W0P from 2 similar outings) must be noted despite the talent marker of two earlier wins.

runners_data.name: Golden Strike
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 5-year-old wears a visor and was a course-and-distance winner on good ground most recently; Oisin Orr partners a horse who naturally wants to race up with the pace but the redistribution means that position may not be available — the good-ground form (2W2P) is nonetheless the most directly relevant stat here.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's 3-year-old has a string of placed efforts behind it including a win over 8f on good going; Jonny Peate from a hold-up position will need a genuine gallop to close from the rear, and the tendency to post 6th-place finishes repeatedly (six in the last seven runs) is a pattern worth noting.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Ruth Jefferson's 3-year-old has consistent placed form at 7-8f on good ground (2W4P from 11); Billy Garritty rides and will look to sit prominently — the low trainer 14-day strike rate (0/1) is minor, and this horse's profile as a honest good-ground performer makes it one of the more straightforward prominent profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Delinquent
runners_data.note: K R Burke has strong recent form (13/46 in 14 days) and this 3-year-old has won twice at 8f — the horse naturally wants to race with the pace, but being pushed toward midfield by the sheer number of prominent types ahead of it is a genuine handicap; Cam Hardie will need to be adaptable.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — no assessment applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Nature is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard, will be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled tempo over York's straight mile. The field behind her contains a glut of naturally prominent types — Jimmy Speaking, Sujet, Frankies Dream, Zennor Storm and Blue To Blue will all contest the early positions, while Cadarn, Eligible, Golden Strike and Delinquent are genuine prominent racers who cannot all get their favoured spot and will be shuffled into midfield against their nature. The rear contingent of Wahdan, Darkness, Andesite and Tailgunner Joe will track through the field but must find a strong enough closing run to reel in a front-runner operating over a genuine mile trip for the first time. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate — Wild Nature is best-placed to hold her position, with Zennor Storm, Jimmy Speaking and Frankies Dream most likely to secure the prime berths just off the lead; this race shape favours those sitting close to a manageable pace with enough stamina to sustain momentum through the final two furlongs, giving the on-pace hold-a-position profile the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Soft Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Nature dictates a comfortable gallop and the pace never truly quickens until the final furlong, those sitting close to the tempo hold a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: If Wild Nature dictates a comfortable gallop and the pace never truly quickens until the final furlong, those sitting close to the tempo hold a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage behind Wild Nature forces a faster early pace than expected, the genuine midfield closers are unleashed for a late charge.
scenarios.body: If the prominent scrimmage behind Wild Nature forces a faster early pace than expected, the genuine midfield closers are unleashed for a late charge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Blows Race Open
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of jostling prominent types creates a ragged, fast early tempo, the race becomes a stamina test that suits those who can settle and close.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of jostling prominent types creates a ragged, fast early tempo, the race becomes a stamina test that suits those who can settle and close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Clear Field
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Nature and one well-placed rival establish a clear lead and the midfield fails to close the gap through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Wild Nature and one well-placed rival establish a clear lead and the midfield fails to close the gap through the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Wild Nature and Oisin Murphy: if Murphy is allowed to slip the field on a comfortable lead through the first four furlongs, the race may be functionally over before the straight begins — watch the opening quarter-mile fractions closely.

Cadarn, Eligible, Golden Strike and Delinquent are all genuine prominent racers crammed into the same starting shape; watch the first two furlongs for crowding and bumping that could compromise any or all of these runners' chances before the race has truly begun.

Zennor Storm's good-ground form is a live concern — both prior runs on comparable ground produced 9th and 10th, and if the track rides quicker than expected, Tom Marquand may find this horse unable to replicate its earlier winning form.

Tailgunner Joe has finished 6th or worse in six of his last seven starts despite posting a win at 8f earlier in his career — watch whether Jonny Peate can find a different gear from this horse or whether the pattern of mid-pack finishes simply continues.

Frankies Dream's hood and consistent placed record at 8-9f on good ground makes it one to monitor through the early stages — if Clifford Lee settles this horse just off Wild Nature's shoulder without expending early energy, it becomes a meaningful player in the closing stages.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Manatee Mehmas
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field; David Nolan rides for David O'Meara and the horse won over this exact 5f/Good combination last time out, but the STYLE_FIT flag is genuine — racing slightly out of its optimal role as a lead horse under pressure from 14 prominent types means even a clean lead does not guarantee a comfortable experience late.|

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey yard at 7/69 in the last 14 days suggests a quieter spell; hold-up horse who has struggled to land a blow in 15 runners at 6f Good recently and drops back to 5f, where the short trip over York's straight course may actually help him if the pace collapses, though his form string of 27-900 demands caution.|

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's yard at just 1/15 in the 14-day window is a flag, but the horse has an outstanding record at this 5f/Good combination — 12 runs, 2 wins and 9 places — and Oliver Stammers gets the ride; prominent style ideally suited to the expected single-setter race shape.|

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: K R Burke's prominent racer has recent Good-ground form reading 12-2-5-1-4 over 5f but most of those placed efforts came on Soft or slower ground; the 4-from-6 Good hit-rate is misleading given the single win came on Soft, and this field is deeper than his recent wins encountered.|

runners_data.name: Fortification
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's consistent prominent runner — form figures 3-2-4-1-4-3 show he hits the frame repeatedly over 5f on Good ground; Ben Robinson gets a clear chance from a horse with proven winning ability at this trip and the race shape should allow him to track Manatee Mehmas in an ideal position.|

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's 3-year-old has placed at 3f and 4f on Good over 5f twice in the last fortnight and Neil Callan rides; the horse is operating as a prominent type whose best efforts have come at the head of affairs, and this smaller 129lb weight gives a degree of edge over some rivals.|

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty rides for Michael and David Easterby — yard at 5/31 in the last 14 days which is respectable — and the horse has two wins over this shorter trip on Soft/Standard, though its 5f Good record shows only a single placed effort from five tries, which tempers enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's hold-up horse with two wins on Good over 5f in recent history; the 21-day break is not a significant flag for this yard and the horse has the profile to finish powerfully if the field bunches — Scenario C is where his chance lives, and Mark Winn should be able to find cover.|

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for Katie Scott — a significant jockey upgrade — and this horse has three 5f Good wins in its last eight runs; it is a natural front-running type whose redistribution to midfield reflects field congestion rather than ability, and Murphy's tactical intelligence makes it the most likely of the displaced prominent horses to reclaim a forward berth.|

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: David Marnane's runner has won twice but both victories came on Soft or Standard surfaces, not Good; a true front-running type who will find limited space at the head of affairs in a 15-runner sprint, meaning Robbie Colgan will face early decisions about whether to force the issue or accept a more restrained position.|

runners_data.name: Front Line Fury
runners_data.note: George Scott's horse shaped well for a second-place finish at 6f/Standard last time but Good-ground form over 5f has been disappointing — six runs, no wins, one place; a genuine prominent racer who is mapped to midfield due to field congestion, and Tom Marquand will need luck in running from a position that does not suit the horse's natural rhythm.|

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is prolific at 7/92 in 14 days and Sean Kirrane has a good record in big-field sprints; however, the form string -84380 tells a stark story, and this horse's best effort (third) came at 6f on Good — dropping to 5f York with a congested race shape and eight runs at similar level without a win makes this a difficult case to build.|

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: The tongue-tie is the headline equipment note and Tim Easterby's yard is warm; however, eight runs on Good over 5f have produced two wins but the recent sequence of 9-3-5-7-6 shows declining form, and as a natural prominent type pushed into midfield by field congestion, James Sullivan will need to work hard to recover her preferred forward pitch.|

runners_data.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's prominent horse has a recent win at 5f on Soft and solid Standard form but a 0-from-2 record on Good specifically is worth noting against a field with stronger Good-ground credentials; Silvestre De Sousa is a high-class booking, and the horse's natural front-running instincts will be constrained by the number of similar types in this field.|

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's filly has won twice over this 5f Good combination and Cam Hardie gets the ride from the rail; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse in front of her, and with just one confirmed pace-setter setting a manageable tempo, she may find the leader and prominent horses too close to reel in.|

races.paceDynamic: Manatee Mehmas is the confirmed front-runner here and, with just one horse confirmed to want to lead from the gate, the early pace should be controlled and sustainable rather than frenetic — a single-setter tempo over York's straight 5f on Good ground that will not burn the field off but will keep the race honest throughout. Behind Manatee Mehmas, a cluster of prominent types including Schrodinger's Cat, Fortification, Our Cody and Shes Got A Brother will press forward and compete for the favoured positions just off the pace, creating a compact early order with very little dead air. This field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate: Naana's Shadow, Allsortz, Front Line Fury, Go Vince Go, Hanney Girl and Alfa Duplicate are all natural pace-pressing horses who are likely to find themselves racing in a more crowded midfield group than their natural style demands, with Naana's Shadow (Oisin Murphy, 5 wins, strong York-distance form) and Allsortz the most likely to hustle and reclaim a genuine prominent pitch. The race shape — a single controlled leader, steady fractions on Good ground, a tight pack behind — firmly favours horses racing prominently just off the pace who have both the tactical speed to track and the finishing kick to override a measured tempo, rather than genuine hold-up horses who will need something to go wrong in front.

scenarios.body: If the pack bunches so tightly early that natural prominent types are genuinely squeezed back and runners with real late speed can thread through

watchPoints.text: Naana's Shadow — Oisin Murphy's jockey upgrade on a horse with three 5f Good wins is the single biggest angle in this race; if Murphy can force his way to a prominent pitch from the gate rather than accepting a midfield slot, this horse becomes a serious danger to the field.

Schrodinger's Cat — outstanding 12-run, 9-place record at 5f on Good ground is hard to dismiss; if the race runs to the prominent-stalker shape, Oliver Stammers's mount has the tactical profile to track Manatee Mehmas and quicken past late.

Pace scramble in the first furlong — with six natural prominent types unable to secure their preferred spot, there is a genuine risk of a ragged early rush as horses like Allsortz, Front Line Fury and Go Vince Go break sharply and clash for position, which could unsettle the expected controlled tempo.

Manatee Mehmas's stamina under pressure — having led alone, any late headwinds from a tight-pressing group behind it could see the confirmed front-runner shorten stride inside the final furlong, opening the door for prominent horses travelling comfortably in second or third.

Rotokura Belle and Mighty Magnus — both genuine hold-up types whose chances hinge on the pace proving genuinely fast enough to set up a late run; on the expected pace evidence of a single controlled leader, both face a significant tactical hurdle and would need an untypically fast tempo to justify confidence.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Criterion Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Held-up type who needs a genuinely run race to produce her best work; Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has three placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs but no win, and her last two outings on Soft have been disappointing — the step back to Good is a plus but she remains vulnerable if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with a strong record on Good going (13/15 sim-going runs, one win, four places) and ran second over this exact course and distance recently; Oisin Orr takes the ride and this combination suits a strongly-run 7f more than a messy tactical affair.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: The class act of the field at OR 115 and Andrew Balding's horse has won twice over 7f and 1m on Good, making him well suited to conditions; he is the lone front-runner who will control tempo and his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects that this is his natural role — he should get it uncontested here, which is his biggest asset.

runners_data.name: Qirat
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's prominent-style runner has form over a mile rather than 7f and comes here with a tongue-tie; his sim-going record of 7/15 is modest, his last run on Soft was a poor 7th, and the drop in trip looks a slight concern — he is likely to track Never So Brave but lacks the recent form to suggest he can go with the leader when it matters.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: William Knight's mare has an excellent record on Good going (14/15, six wins), winning three of her last four in that condition, but she is a natural prominent runner who is unlikely to get that position with Never So Brave in the field — her chance is tempered by being squeezed out of her preferred early berth, though her Good-ground speed makes her dangerous in a scramble.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old is lightly raced (only six runs) but has won twice on Good going at 7f, and Tom Marquand's experience gives him tactical options; he carries the lightest weight at 125lbs and his recency — last ran just seven days ago — suggests freshness, though like Royal Velvet he is a natural front-of-field type who will find Never So Brave has taken his ground.

races.paceDynamic: Never So Brave is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals and no genuine pace rival to push him, he should secure a comfortable lead and control tempo from the outset on Good ground at York. Saber Strike and Royal Velvet are both natural prominent racers but, with Never So Brave already filling that role, they are likely to be shuffled into midfield positions that do not reflect their true style — neither can simultaneously lead with Never So Brave. Balmacara and Chicago Critic are genuine hold-up types who will settle in behind and rely on a strong finish from the rear, while Qirat has prominent tendencies but has been outpaced at this level recently. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Never So Brave is almost certain to lead, Saber Strike is the most likely to press for second position given youth and recency, with Royal Velvet forced widest back. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader on genuine Good turf over 7f — strongly favours horses that can race prominently or press the pace, as the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to reel in a class front-runner who dictates throughout.

scenarios.title: Never So Brave Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Never So Brave leads unchallenged and sets a measured, controlled pace that suits his stamina and class advantage.
scenarios.body: If Never So Brave leads unchallenged and sets a measured, controlled pace that suits his stamina and class advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Late; Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Never So Brave sets a pace that is unusually strong for this small field, burning off prominent types and leaving the race open to closers over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Never So Brave sets a pace that is unusually strong for this small field, burning off prominent types and leaving the race open to closers over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Assert
scenarios.trigger: If Saber Strike or Royal Velvet manage to press Never So Brave hard enough to unsettle him, creating a contested pace that blows up the field.
scenarios.body: If Saber Strike or Royal Velvet manage to press Never So Brave hard enough to unsettle him, creating a contested pace that blows up the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess; Form Reversal
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a crawl with a bunch finish and late sprint, negating pace shape entirely and rewarding pure sprint ability.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at a crawl with a bunch finish and late sprint, negating pace shape entirely and rewarding pure sprint ability.

watchPoints.text: Never So Brave's ability to secure uncontested lead without pressure from Saber Strike or Royal Velvet is the single biggest race-shaping factor — watch the first two furlongs to see if any rival challenges him for the front.

Saber Strike and Royal Velvet are both true prominent types who cannot both race where they want — watch for scrimmaging in the early stages as jockeys scramble for position, which could compromise both runners' chances.

Chicago Critic wears a hood (hg:p) and is a hold-up horse who will be detached early; if Never So Brave sets only a modest pace, watch for Oisin Orr being caught in no-man's land rather than the strong gallop he needs.

The Good going at York over 7f has been confirmed across multiple races today — no significant bias reported, so watch for whether the pace quickens early (suits closers) or is held steady (suits the front-runner).

Royal Velvet ran just nine days ago — watch her in the paddock and early on track for any sign of residual fatigue, as her rapid return could be a positive freshness angle or a concern depending on how she moves.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine pace-setter, six-year-old in good form at this trip, but tagged with a modest style-fit rating as a confirmed prominent runner stepping into a front-running role — De Sousa gets on well with the type and 35 days fresh is ideal, though solo front-running over 1m6f leaves it vulnerable if rivals up the tempo.

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old is lightly raced and progressive, winning twice over shorter good ground trips, and steps up sharply in distance here — 62 days off may need a smooth lead to warm into the race, but Cian Horgan's 5lb claim is a meaningful financial advantage in a handicap at this level.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago and carries the fitness edge, with a course-and-distance win over 18f in good going underlining the stamina credentials — Oisin Orr takes a strong spare ride, and the headgear note (tv) is worth watching as the hood has featured in recent outings; trainer Keatley fires from distance with a solid 14-day strike rate.

runners_data.name: Imperial Sovereign
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this five-year-old who has placed consistently without winning in similar company on good and standard going — trainer Kirby's 14-day figures show no runners returned, and the hold-up style requires a truly run race over this trip, which is not guaranteed with an uncontested leader.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old veteran has form at this distance but recent runs show persistent out-of-frame efforts on good ground over 1m6f and beyond — Sean Kirrane takes over and Easterby has a high-volume 14-day presence, but the form string of 560603 and a 10th last time at this distance on good ground make it hard to upgrade.

runners_data.name: Terrorise
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old wears a visor and has struggled badly in recent starts, finishing deep in the field at 1m6f on good ground — naturally a hold-up horse but the redistribution note reflects that this field already has more rearward types than can all settle where they wish, compounding an already difficult profile; 50 days off adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: A four-year-old by breeding and form that has operated at shorter trips (7-9f), stepping up sharply in distance here — Garritty partners a horse whose headgear note (h) suggests keenness management, and while it has won on soft ground at sprint trips, the 1m6f on good turf is a significant ask; naturally a hold-up type but likely to find itself further forward than ideal in this race.

runners_data.name: My Ballyquinn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's lightly-raced three-year-old has a strong record on good ground with a win and three placings from five runs on that surface — the unknown style tag is notable given limited data, and Mark Winn has a solid book of rides for the yard; the step from 1m2f to 1m6f is the critical unknown, but the form figures of 2-1-4-1-2 on good ground are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Who's Lope
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on Andrew Balding's lightly-raced three-year-old, who has won at 1m2f and placed at 1m4f on good ground — only three career runs but the profile is steeply progressive, and Murphy's involvement for a trainer with a healthy 14-day strike rate makes this a horse of significant interest as it steps into staying company for the first time.

races.paceDynamic: Rock N Roll Pinkie is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger likely to push them hard from the outset over 1m6f on Good ground at York, the expectation is a measured, controlled gallop from the front with the race effectively run to suit a prominent-tracking style. Talismans Time and Secret Force will look to press or sit just off the leader, meaning the front of the race will be well populated, leaving the hold-up contingent — Imperial Sovereign, Gibside, and Who's Lope — with ground to make up in the straight. Terrorise and Draupnir are genuine hold-up operators by nature but, with a field already stacked toward the rear, they are mapped to midfield — the field carries more hold-up types than can all naturally settle at the back, and those two are most likely to be shuffled into a middle-pack position rather than securing their true rearward berth. The race shape — a sustainable, uncontested gallop over a long flat mile and six — most favours horses who can travel prominently, conserve energy through the race, and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is run at a rhythm that rewards those travelling close to the pace.
scenarios.body: If Rock N Roll Pinkie dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is run at a rhythm that rewards those travelling close to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie's uncontested lead proves too generous and the pack never seriously challenges before the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If Rock N Roll Pinkie's uncontested lead proves too generous and the pack never seriously challenges before the furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Young Stayer Swamps Them
scenarios.trigger: If Who's Lope or My Ballyquinn travel powerfully from midfield and their improving profile gives them the reserves to overhaul the prominent runners late.
scenarios.body: If Who's Lope or My Ballyquinn travel powerfully from midfield and their improving profile gives them the reserves to overhaul the prominent runners late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses in the middle stages and a true rear-runner gets a dream unobstructed run up the outside.
scenarios.body: If the pace genuinely collapses in the middle stages and a true rear-runner gets a dream unobstructed run up the outside.

watchPoints.text: Who's Lope is lightly raced and steeply progressive — watch for Oisin Murphy to hunt a position just off the pace and produce a smooth, powerful run in the straight that could overwhelm more exposed rivals.

Draupnir's natural trip is 7-9f and this is 1m6f — if it fails to settle or gets bumped wide in a field of nine, the stamina reserve may simply not be there; watch for signs of distress entering the final half-mile.

Talismans Time is 62 days off — if Cian Horgan is unable to find a rhythm early and the horse is flat to warm into the race, the promising recent form over shorter trips may not translate immediately at this distance.

Rock N Roll Pinkie's front-running role carries an inherent risk if any runner tests from early — watch whether Talismans Time or Secret Force presses closer than expected in the first half-mile, as any pressure could undermine the controlled gallop scenario.

Secret Force ran only six days ago — monitor the market and paddock for signs of freshness or fatigue given the short turnaround; if sharp and on its toes, the fitness advantage over rivals returning after breaks is real.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Sprint Handicap

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Front foot in nature, Ben Robinson should push for a prominent pitch early; recent form shows a drop to 6f after staying trips and the sim-going record is thin, but York's straight six suits a horse that travels prominently and this trainer has a sharp 1-from-5 in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by preference, Oisin McSweeney will need to exercise patience in a race this congested at the rear end; seven York-going runs show consistency without a win here, but the 6f trip has previously produced a place and a closing run through tired rivals is this horse's best chance.|

runners_data.name: Hallo Spaceboy
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking is immediately significant for a horse that has won and placed repeatedly over 6f on Good; 50 days off is manageable for Ed Walker, who has three from 39 in the 14-day window, and a position tracking second or third could allow Murphy to exploit rivals scrimmaging for space ahead.|

runners_data.name: Rikki Tiki Tavi
runners_data.note: Off 70 days and returning to 6f Good after a string of below-par efforts; the one win on this going and distance combination is a positive marker, but the trainer's 14-day strike rate is modest and Kevin Stott will need to be fortunate with a clean run from the hold-up position.|

runners_data.name: Invincible Boy
runners_data.note: Three-run career showing two places and a win over 6f on Good, making this the most relevant form profile in the field; Richard and Peter Fahey send this horse out on 81 days off, which is a slight concern, but Oisin Orr is a sharp judge of pace and a mid-prominent berth suits perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with headgear (h) worn, William Pyle rides for a small yard with a single winner from 18 in the 14-day window; the sim-going record reads 10 from 15 in terms of win-or-place positions suggesting modest consistency, and this horse needs a truly messy race to be involved.|

runners_data.name: Vidmiyr
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners a horse whose recent form over 7-8f on Good and Standard surfaces shows a win and multiple places; stepping back to 6f is the key question — the style is prominent and the 15-day turnaround is short but the trainer has fired in one from 17 recently.|

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Returning from 345 days off — by far the longest absence in the field — as a now-three-year-old who was placed four times at two; the form on Good ground is strong in raw terms but the layoff is a major flag, and Sean Kirrane will need this horse to produce a career-best first time back.|

runners_data.name: Mr Noble
runners_data.note: Only two career runs both on Standard ground at a track that differs markedly from York's straight 6f on Good; Clifford Lee is capable and K R Burke sends them out in good shape (10 from 48 in 14 days) but the absence of any turf-good evidence is a genuine unknown in this field.|

runners_data.name: Million Gold
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand picks up the ride on a horse that won over this C&D equivalent on Standard; in truth a prominent racer by instinct but with six others wanting that berth, Appleby's runner may find itself squeezed wider than ideal, and the 154-day absence adds another layer of uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Percy's Star
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, De Sousa's task is to steal a march from the gates and control the fractions; the horse has a 1W2P record in four York-going runs, handles this trip, and wears headgear (p) — if allowed an uncontested lead this is a live each-way proposition at minimum.|

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Shows a pattern of consistent placed efforts without winning, and the hold-up style means Rawlinson must navigate traffic in a chaotic midfield; 15 days between runs and a trainer with two from 16 recently suggest the team is active — the 6f Good trip has yielded a place before.|

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: John Butler's charge has a headline win on Good over 6f but recent form reads 6-6-2 and the overall Good-going record is 10 from 13 starts in terms of placed positions — moderate at best; this horse's natural hold-up style means Marco Ghiani may find the prominent chaos ahead actually plays into his hands if gaps appear late.|

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners a horse that has been busily campaigned (10 days since last run) by the productive Tim Easterby yard (6 from 96 in 14 days); by instinct a horse that wants to be in contention early, though the congested prominent group means it may be forced wider or deeper than Hardie would like, which blunts its best chance.|

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: James Sullivan rides on a fresh eight-day turnaround for Michael and David Easterby; a natural hold-up horse whose two recent placed efforts came on Standard, and the York Good-going record shows nothing better than seventh — the combination of trip, going and redistribution away from its natural position makes this one of the harder cases to make.|

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Star is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the outside, Silvestre De Sousa should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without being harassed into an unsustainable tempo. Behind him, six runners — including Evening Blues, Hallo Spaceboy, Invincible Boy, Vidmiyr, Bleep Test and Mr Noble — all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the rail and the first two or three lengths off the leader between the 6f start and the two-furlong marker. This prominent-runner glut means traffic and positional friction are near-certain around the 2-3f pole, which will suit any horse who can settle just behind the scrimmage and accelerate cleanly through gaps. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can physically accommodate; Million Gold and Bye Law are genuine prominent horses who are most likely to be shuffled back against their will, while Logi Bear and Von Trotter are true hold-up horses who may find themselves further forward than ideal due to the chaotic middle-pack dynamics. The race shape — a solo leader, organised early, followed by a bunched prominent group fighting for slots — strongly favours horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile who possess a clean turn of foot on good ground and can exploit the inevitable gaps as rivals check and shuffle at the business end.

scenarios.body: If the prominent battle implodes completely and genuine closers get a clear run through on the inside or outside in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Star is the only true front-runner and if De Sousa is slow out of the stalls or bumped at the break, the entire race dynamic collapses — watch for a clean exit from the gates.|

Six prominent-style runners — Evening Blues, Hallo Spaceboy, Invincible Boy, Vidmiyr, Bleep Test and Mr Noble — are all angling for the same real estate two to three furlongs out; expect significant checking and bumping in the 4-2f zone that could fatally compromise one or more of them.|

Bleep Test returns from 345 days off and any market move from its morning price should be noted as a trainer confidence signal — Tim Easterby's record suggests horses are fit when they run, but the layoff is extreme.|

Million Gold and Bye Law, genuine prominent horses mapped to midfield, may find themselves in no-man's land if they push forward into traffic or stay back against their instincts — watch how Marquand and Hardie play the first furlong to judge whether these horses can factor.|

Invincible Boy has raced only three times and connections are sending a lightly-raced horse into a 15-runner handicap over the most competitive distance in sprinting — inexperience in a big field at the 2f pole could be the difference between winning and finishing out of the frame.|

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Front-runner with back-to-back wins over 10-12f on Good ground recently; sets the pace here by default and with a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he's racing slightly out of his natural role, his chance is most likely to materialise if allowed a clean lead rather than being pressed.

runners_data.name: Machete
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has shown no winning form in 15 similar-going runs; 57 days off and a history confined to Southwell AW handicaps at this trip makes the transition to Good turf at York a steep ask.

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up runner whose entire recent profile is built around 7f on Good ground — stepping to 1m2½f is a significant distance jump and the 0W3P record in similar going does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Double Parked
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a sound record at 8-10f on Good ground, two placed efforts in last five; Tim Easterby's yard is among the most active in 14 days (8/106) and the tongue-tie is retained — represents a key market mover to monitor.

runners_data.name: Ben Lawers
runners_data.note: Irish raider who tends to race prominently; tongue-tie applied and 48 days between runs, but the 1m form figures on Good ground are modest and this longer 1m2½f trip represents the acid test of his stamina.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist at 7-8f on soft/good ground with visor and tongue-tie; nothing in the form or distance profile suggests she can strike from off the pace here, and 0W0P in 15 similar-going runs is a stark number.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who found her only win over 9f on Good — the step to 1m2½f suits and the 1W3P record in similar going gives her a credible profile if able to get a clear run from the rear; jockey's claim of 5lb helps.

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: In his natural races he settles deep and finishes late, but here he is pushed into a midfield berth by the volume of hold-up types; the 1W4P similar-going record is respectable but the compromised position makes delivering that finish harder.

runners_data.name: Urban Road
runners_data.note: Strong closer who has placed twice at 10f on Good ground — the reality is that with five hold-up types crowding the rear, he is mapped into a midfield spot that is not his preferred starting point, blunting his natural late run.

runners_data.name: Caph Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at 10f on Good ground, one win and two places in similar conditions; Mark Rimell's small team (T14: 0/5) is quiet but the horse's profile — tongue-tie, consistent form figures — suits a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Runs prominently with hood and tongue-tie, has placed twice over 10f on Good; James Owen is in excellent 14-day form (9/49) and this horse's ability to travel in touch gives it a live chance if the pace is controlled.

runners_data.name: Theme Park
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse forced into midfield by the field's configuration; 232 days off the track is a major concern, the AW Southwell form at 8f does not obviously translate, and the style compromise makes a winning performance a tall order on return.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Has won at 9f on Good and placed twice at 10-12f; a natural closer whose placement into midfield blunts his late-race weapon — the form on Good ground is there but the structural disadvantage is real and must be discounted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up type with two wins over 11-12f at Goodwood on Good and AW; the form at this trip is solid and the horse's tactical versatility means it can adapt if the pace is uneven, though the OR of 61 faces a stiff test against higher-rated rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Hengest is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to push him hard from the gates, he should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over the 1m2½f trip on Good ground at York. Double Parked, Ben Lawers, Caph Star, No Knee Never and Sisterandbrother will all look to press or sit prominently, meaning the pace is real but Hengest can control its tempo rather than being dragged into a war. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Glistening Nights, Urban Road, Theme Park and Spirit Catcher are all natural closers who will be forced to race further forward than ideal, compromising their finishing kicks. With a genuine but controlled pace, horses settled just off the leader in a prominent or close-tracking position are best placed to exploit the even tempo and pounce in the straight; pure closers relying on a strong pace to generate momentum look structurally disadvantaged here.

watchPoints.text: Hengest's early gallop tempo is the race's defining variable — if he quickens from the gates and steals a clear lead before the field settles, prominent challengers Double Parked and Ben Lawers must commit immediately or risk being left too far back.

Pearl Eye and Spirit Catcher are the most likely beneficiaries of a strong pace, but with Urban Road, Theme Park and Glistening Nights also crowding the rear-to-midfield zone, traffic and interference in the straight is a significant risk for all late runners.

Theme Park has been off the track for 232 days — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the parade ring and early stages, as an unfit reappearance from a hold-up position would leave this runner with no viable path to the frame.

James Owen's yard (T14: 9/49) is in sharp form and No Knee Never carries hood and tongue-tie in a race where controlled pace suits prominent types — monitor market moves on this runner in the hour before the off.

Double Parked runs for Tim Easterby (8/106 in 14 days, one of the most active yards on the card) and has placed three times at 8f on Good; a step to 1m2½f is untested at the highest level — watch whether connections are bullish about the trip in market behaviour.
